name: Theodor W. Adorno
role: German philosopher, sociologist and Frankfurt School critical theorist, 1903–1969
summary: Adorno criticized capitalist domination and commercial mass culture while defending critical autonomy and democratic freedoms. His writings opposed sexual repression, patriarchal gender ideals and renewed nationalist persecution.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Acknowledged criticisms but expressly said society cannot dispense with division of labor.

alienated-labor.rationale: Described heteronomous work subordinating people to apparatuses.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Condemned dismissing suffering because victims are animals.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Rejected melting-pot assimilation in favor of reconciled differences.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Explicitly recognized capitalism’s ability to postpone collapse.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Acknowledged productive development enabling liberation from hunger.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Criticized manufactured consumption and pseudo-individuality as substitutes for fulfilled needs.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Denounced Paragraph 175 and its blackmail consequences.

democracy-best.rationale: Defended substantive democracy despite shortcomings and immaturity.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Required lived democratic freedom beyond formal rules.

direct-action.rationale: Supported specific demonstrations and blockades while rejecting actionism and demands to subordinate theory to activism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Envisioned emancipation around needs and eliminating hunger.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rejected compulsory bonds and obedience to collectives.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Participated in opposition to German emergency legislation expanding exceptional state powers.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Defended autonomous, independent judgment against pressures producing standardized, conformist individuals.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Defended equal freedom without demanding identical characteristics.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Described ideal femininity as masculine society’s product.

gradual-change.rationale: Rejected the sufficiency of minor adjustments, while supporting criminal-law reforms and student-driven university reform.

harm-principle.rationale: Required demonstrated harm to justify sexual restrictions.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Rejected minimization and denial of Nazi extermination.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Blamed oppressive social relations rather than technology itself.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Condemned the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: His letters supported Israel’s survival as a refuge for persecuted Jews, without specifying territorial boundaries.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Retained Marx’s framework but questioned surplus-value theory’s adequacy.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Condemned brothel closures and persecution of prostitutes.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Argued commodified entertainment manufactures adaptation to domination.

means-match-ends.rationale: Demanded emancipatory praxis avoid reproducing oppressive methods.

national-rebirth.rationale: Identified nationalist revival movements with renewed sadism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Traced feminine subordination to institutionalized male domination.

person-over-state.rationale: Condemned subordinating individual rights to state necessity.

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: Adorno tells students to ask cui bono of texts, citing Hobbes serving the restoration of the monarchy, but says this must not become a crude theory that every text is merely an expression of interests.

premarital-sex.rationale: Opposed compulsory chastity and patriarchal sexual prohibitions.

production-for-use.rationale: Contrasted genuine needs with profit-directed production.

reification.rationale: Described economic apparatuses dominating their human creators.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Rejected adult pornography censorship without demonstrated harm.

sacred-nation.rationale: Adorno calls nationalism the characteristic form of absurd opinion and a full-blown ideology that has lost its real basis, so he rejects treating the nation as a sacred community.

separated-powers.rationale: Explicitly defended reciprocal executive, legislative, judicial checks.

space-expansion.rationale: Rejected conquering distant stars as emancipation’s goal.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Presented interventionist government as capitalism’s collective defender.

strong-leader.rationale: Condemned the desire for prominent personalities to direct collective affairs.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Made independent criticism constitutive of democratic freedom.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Denied technical development alone overcomes social domination.

technology-design-reflects-political-int.rationale: The co-authored culture-industry chapter says technology gains power over society through the power of those whose economic position is strongest, and calls technical rationality the rationality of domination.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rejected workplace integration alone as women’s emancipation.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: In the 1956 discussions Adorno says "we must not succumb to the ideology of work" and asks how work comes to be an absolute, though he also grants that happiness is twinned with work.

notes: No institutional blueprint inferred from Marxist affiliation. Criticism of Soviet domination does not establish endorsement of capitalist restoration. His late interview permits resistance to dictatorship while opposing actionism in West Germany. The labor-value question remains contested within his own argument. Gender criticism does not establish specific voting, inheritance or marriage statutes. Melting-pot criticism concerns coerced sameness, not racial segregation. Sexual-law arguments do not establish modern marriage or gender-identity policies. Later reports of letters receive medium confidence; Horkheimer and Marcuse are not substituted for Adorno. All remaining nulls reviewed across ten themes.
